About this document


This document provides the teaching content for Health Studies Years 11–13 of the
New Zealand Curriculum.

Progress and assessment information for Health Studies Years 11–13 is still in
development. Once that is completed, Health Studies Years 11–13 is proposed to be
made by the Minister of Education as a National Curriculum Statement under section
90(1)(a) of the Education and Training Act 2020.

It is proposed that, once made and published in the New Zealand Gazette, schools
who offer Health Studies Years 11–13 will be required to start using it in Year 11 from
1 January 2028, in Year 12 from 1 January 2029, and in Year 13 from 1 January
2030.

This document will be replaced with the official version made under the Act and
published in the New Zealand Gazette once that has occurred.

Purpose statement                                            He oranga ngākau, he pikinga waiora.        Positive feelings in your heart will raise your sense of self-worth.




  In Health Studies, students are taught about the complex factors that influence                 Health Studies leads to pathways in health sciences and related fields, such as
  personal and community health and well-being. This includes examining health-                   community services, policy, technology, environment, and civic roles.
  related issues such as nutrition, mental health, sexual and reproductive health,
  navigating the digital world, relationships, and global health challenges, and
  considering how these issues intersect across diverse communities and contexts.
  They are taught how to apply critical thinking and ethical decision-making to
  analyse and evaluate health practices, policies, and systems, developing the
  capabilities needed to respond to health needs at personal, community, and
  societal levels.

Students are taught disciplinary knowledge about health and well-being across
physical, mental, and societal dimensions. Students identify and explain key
concepts, models, terminology, and frameworks used in Health Studies, including
approaches to health, determinants of health, health promotion, rights and
responsibilities, relationships, well-being, nutrition, and international health issues.
Health Studies provides students with the knowledge and practices to analyse health-
related issues, situations, data, and systems using health concepts, models, and
evidence, and evaluate health information, evidence, policies, practices, and
interventions using critical and reflective reasoning. This disciplinary knowledge helps
students explain relationships, compare approaches, anticipate consequences, and
propose reasoned responses to complex health issues. They can then also
communicate health-related thinking clearly and appropriately using Health Studies
language, representations, and conventions.
As students progress through Years 11–13, they are taught to develop the capability
to organise, analyse, evaluate, and independently integrate evidence and
perspectives to justify conclusions and recommendations in written form. This
enables them to purposefully shape health messages and arguments for different
audiences, contexts, and purposes, demonstrating ethical awareness, clarity of
reasoning, critical literacy, and respect for diverse perspectives.

 Disciplinary writing

 Focus: the use of writing to reflect the ways in which knowledge is organised, analysed, and communicated within the discipline.
 In Health Studies, students produce writing that evaluates health concepts in relation to individual and community needs and goals. They construct texts that explain and
 advocate for safety, health, and well-being for different audiences, and plan strategies for improving health outcomes using evidence, reflection, and understanding of health and
 well-being concepts.
